Master of Nursing 4+1 Program

  • You are here →
  • Course Catalog
  • Nursing
  • Master of Nursing 4+1

  Download Catalog as PDF

The Master of Nursing is a 4+1 program is designed to encourage Midway undergraduates to complete their MSN at Midway and provides students with a streamlined educational path while ensuring they meet all requirements for both their undergraduate and graduate degrees.

Undergraduate students admitted to this program will be permitted to take two of the three MSN courses, NSG 510 Role Transition, NSG 520 Evidence Based Practice, NSG 530 Quality Improvement and Safety their senior year. Students in these courses take the same class as MSN students and are in the courses with MSN students. The courses will count towards their graduate degree. Students participating in the 4+1 program will complete 120 hours in their undergraduate degree plus the 6 hours of graduate coursework, then complete 30 hours in the graduate degree through the completion of a graduate concentration of their choice. 

Program admission requirements

Students must apply to the 4+1 program and be accepted during their junior year. To be eligible, they must have:

1. 90 hours of undergraduate coursework completed

2. 3.0 Cumulative GPA

Application for the 4+1 Program is hosted in SharePoint on the registrar’s page here: 4 + 1 Application

At the end of their junior year the student must apply to the MSN program

Courses

Select two of the three courses below

nsg-510 - Professional Role Transition - 3 hours

nsg-520 - Evidence-Based Nursing - 3 hours

nsg-530 - Quality Improvement and Safety - 3 hours
